newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Kredietbank foreign strategy focused on profit.
newsitem.headline: Kredietbank foreign strategy focused on profit.

text.p: Belgian Kredietbank said on Thursday its foreign expansion strategy was focused on those areas that have the strongest economic growth.

"Our foreign expansion is not focused strongly on Europe. Europe is over-banked and economic growth there is slow," Kredietbank Chief Executive Officer Marcel Cockaerts told a news conference in reply to a question.
"Furthermore, the Belgian economic cycle has usually been in line with the rest of Europe, so we do not spread our risk by being active in Europe," he added.
Kredietbank's approach is in stark contrast to that of Generale Bank, Belgium's biggest bank, which has focused its foreign operations in a 400-kilometre radius around Brussels.
Remi Vermeiren, a member of Kredietbank's executive committee, said foreign activities already contributed about a third of the bank's earnings.
He said this came mainly from activities in Southeast Asia, Ireland, New York and London.
Cockaerts said the foreign expansion strategy was now focused on Southeast Asia, where the bank hopes to open a fourth branch office in Manila in October.
"We hope to triple the number of branches in Southeast Asia in the coming years," he said.
He added that the bank would also continue its expansion in eastern Europe, where it is active in Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
"We want to become the most active Belgian bank in eastern Europe," Cockaerts said.
The bank said on Thursday that its first-half group net profit rose 14.5 percent to 6.69 billion francs from 5.84 billion in the first half of 1995.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6813, Fax 32 2 230 7710
